key_decisions: MPI-584 registered NO new op and bumped NO version: ltxVideoUpscale, ltx_video_upscale.json and ltxSigmasInjector already existed and were verified by MPI-579. The Flow is one descriptor plus one test.
The Flow's media slot role is `inputVideo`, matching the shared op's mediaInputs key — NOT the `video1` its sibling flows use. The flow bends to the op because the op is shared with the plugin.

The three controls are the plugin's `upscale.fields` VERBATIM (prompt empty, denoise UI 0.5 -> sigma 0.675, prompt strength UI 0 -> cfg 1). Two surfaces of one capability with different defaults is a bug nobody reports as one.
No VRAM/frame cap shipped: the graph exposes no knob to cap, so a cap needs a new node plus a control — its own card. The description carries the warning instead.

MPI-585 must NOT build a third compare engine. ComparisonManager + MpiCanvas activeMode 'compare' already do image/video pairs in both directions; MpiCompareOverlay is the History surface. What is duplicated-in-waiting is the video transport + hotkey block living inside that overlay — lift it, and sweep BOTH consumers.

The board's .agents/mpi-kanban/events.jsonl and state/index.json are left UNCOMMITTED on purpose: my lines interleave with the live MPI-504 session's inside one hunk, so that file is theirs to sweep. My card files and board.json are committed.

A Flow is already an MpiOverlay, so MpiCompareOverlay (a full #tool-container takeover with the Stash Pattern) cannot be reused as-is inside one — that is why MPI-585 builds a third surface rather than calling the overlay.

Never take the user's app on :3000. npm run app:isolated picks its own port and profile; kill the process TREE afterwards (TaskStop leaves the Electron running). The isolated instance still shares APP_DOCUMENTS, so a completed Flow run commits a card into a REAL project — that is why the live upscale was left to Fabio.
